parsedVerdict.reasoning: All five use cases deal with orders and stock, so the module covers one concern. But some rules are written more than once instead of living in one place. The Order-to-OrderDto mapping is copied by hand into four use cases. Only PlaceOrderUseCase puts it in a helper (`mapToDto`), and that helper is private, so the other three can't reuse it. UpdateOrderStatusUseCase also keeps its own hard-coded list of valid OrderStatus values. That list belongs to the domain Order entity, which already guards status changes through `transitionTo` and `canBeCancelled`. Keeping a second copy here can drift from the domain: it leaves out any cancelled state, for example. PlaceOrderUseCase also checks order lines (at least one line, quantity above zero) in the use case rather than in the Order entity. That may duplicate rules the Order constructor already enforces, but Order's source isn't included here, so this point is less certain.
